alex_prod: FYI — I'm rolling a refresh of our internal incident comms templates. Goal: clearer sections, single-tone guidelines for internal vs external, consistent placeholders, and short canned snippets for on-call handoffs and support. Draft is here: https://go/docs/incidents/comm-style-draft (WIP). Need feedback by EOD tomorrow. Key constraints: avoid promising firm ETAs, prioritize empathy + actionable steps, keep external updates concise. Proposed root sections:
- Summary (one line)
- Impact (who/what/scale)
- Mitigation / Workaround (what we're doing + any customer steps)
- Next steps & ETA placeholder
- Contact / Runbook links
Placeholders to standardize: <SERVICE>, <REGION>, <ETA>, <WORKAROUND>, <CONTACT>, <POSTMORTEM_LINK>

samira_p: +1 on the structure. A couple suggestions: 1) For external messages use a single-sentence lead, then 1-2 bullets max — customers skim. 2) Tone: use present active voice: 'We are actively working to restore service' is clearer than 'We're investigating'. 3) Add a line "What this means for customers" when impact is partial/limited. Also recommend a short "No action required" template for support to paste. :+1:

 tom_oncall: adding on-call constraints — please include a compact handoff snippet that we can paste into the incident thread during rotations. It should include pager history, actions taken (short bullets), runbook link, current hypothesis, and who to page next. Example snippet I use: 
```
On-call update — 22:04 UTC
- Pager history: pager triggered x3 at 21:50; noise suppressed once.
- Actions taken: restarted svc-worker on node-12; rolled back deploy v3.2.1 -> v3.2.0.
- Current mitigation: traffic routed to fallback cluster in eu-west.
- Hypothesis: regressing kernel changes in driver.
- Next: escalate to infra oncall @liz_sre if error rate doesn't drop by 22:20.
- Runbook: https://go/runbooks/svc-failure
```
This keeps handoffs fast and readable. Also signal if we should notify customers now vs wait for fix.

liz_sre: Agree with the structure. A few more asks from SRE side:
- Add severity-specific language (Sev1 external = total/partial outage language; Sev2 = degraded).
- Standardize the phrase 'no customer action required' and a short 1-line workaround if available.
- Include a short 'internal impact summary' header for adjacent teams (billing, auth, dedupe).
Also we should avoid absolute promises like "service will be restored by <ETA>" — prefer "we expect service to be restored around <ETA>" when uncertain.

grace_support: From Support perspective please add a canned CS response pack we can copy into Zendesk: 1) initial acknowledgement, 2) 30m update template, 3) resolution message with next steps + compensation note if applicable. Example: 
`Thank you for reporting this. We are currently investigating an issue affecting <SERVICE> in <REGION>. Our engineers are working on a fix — we will follow up with updates every 30 minutes or when we have new info.`
Also include a small troubleshooting checklist for agents: check status page, account-specific impact, and escalate reasons.

morgan_pm: Tone note — customers appreciate accountability. I suggest a short 'what we're doing to prevent recurrence' blurb in the postmortem, but avoid promising immediate remediation in status updates. For external communications, offering to "evaluate customer impact and follow up" is safer than committing credits up front.

inc-bot: [incident-bot] New doc PR opened by alex_prod: PR #2417 — draft: comm-style-snippets. Link: https://go/pulls/2417

alex_prod: thanks everyone — I'm going to incorporate these and push an updated draft tonight. Two implementation items: 1) add template variants for Sev1/Sev2/Sev3, 2) add a support quick-copy block, and 3) add the handoff snippet as an internal-only template. Will also include examples for different outage shapes (total outage vs degraded latency).

samira_p: one nit: prefer placeholder `<ETA>` (shorter) vs `<ESTIMATED_RESTORATION>`. Also include a mandatory `Last updated: <TIMESTAMP>` line on the top of external updates.

alex_prod: good call — switching to `<ETA>` and adding `Last updated: <TIMESTAMP>`. I'll update the doc and create a PR for the templates repo. Plan: request 2 reviewer approvals (SRE + Support) before merging. After merge I'll post a short summary in #eng-oncall and tag the oncall rotation.

alex_prod: Draft of the external outage template (WIP):
```
[EXTERNAL] Last updated: <TIMESTAMP>
We are currently experiencing an issue affecting <SERVICE> in <REGION>.
Impact: <short one-liner about who is affected>
What we're doing: <one-line mitigation steps + runbook link>
Workaround: <WORKAROUND or 'No workaround available'>
ETA: <ETA>
Contact: <CONTACT>
```

liz_sre: looks good — maybe add an optional line for 'next update expected in <minutes>' if the incident is ongoing.

grace_support: sample CS initial reply for copy/paste: 
`Hi <CUSTOMER_NAME>, thanks for flagging this. We are aware of an issue affecting <SERVICE>. Our engineers are working on a fix. We will post updates at regular intervals here: <STATUS_PAGE_LINK>. No action is required from you right now. — <AGENT_NAME>`

alex_prod: PR created: https://go/pulls/2417 (includes templates + handoff snippet + CS pack). Please review. I'm aiming to merge by EOD if no blockers.

morgan_pm: minor suggestion for language in the CS pack resolution message: replace 'we will credit' with 'we will evaluate and follow up regarding any compensation' — keeps expectations manageable.

samira_p: reviewed, left two small wording comments in PR. :memo:
